The instant petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed by the petitioner praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 613/2022, registered at Police Station Keshav Puram, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Anand V. Khatri, learned ASC (Crl.) accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioner is present before this Court and has been identified by his counsel Mr. Baldev Raj and Investigating Officer (IO) WSI Kailash from Police Station Keshav Puram, Delhi.

6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner and respondent no. 2 had been solemnized on 09.02.2003 according to Hindu (Sikh) rites, customs and ceremonies at New Delhi Servpal Singh vs State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50941883/
1 and out of this wedlock, one female child was born.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that due to some temperamental differences and matrimonial differences, the complainant/respondent no. 2 left the company of the petitioner and started living separately.

On the complaint of complainant/respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 613/2022 was registered at Police Station Keshav Puram, Delhi, for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC against petitioner.

It is further stated that petitioner and respondent no. 2 have resolved their disputes amicably vide Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) dated 09.11.2022.
7.

On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) dated 09.11.2022.
8.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

9. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 3,50,000/- in two installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 3,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement in second motion.
b. Second/final instalment of Rs.50,000/- to be paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of quashing of FIR before Honble High Court at New Delhi.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 50,000/- today, i.e., 21.03.2023 vide DD No. 243522 drawn on UCO Bank, New Delhi, and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 613/2022, registered at Police Station Keshav Puram, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. The present petition stands disposed of.
14. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
